fields.title: 📖 Knowledge Must Become Visible in Conduct
fields.body:
🖋️ **Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said:**
***“In earlier times a man sought knowledge, and soon its effect was seen in his humility, his way of life, his tongue, his gaze, and his hand.”***
This statement shows that true **knowledge** is not recognized only by many words, books, or discussions. Its effect must become visible in **character**, in the way of life, and in a person’s deeds.
Whoever truly learns becomes **more humble**, more careful with his tongue, and more restrained with his gaze and his hands.
Knowledge should not make a person more arrogant and quarrelsome, but lead him to more **fear of Allah, dignity, and good conduct**.
The Salaf regarded knowledge as **education of the whole person**. The conduct of one who knows should testify that what was learned reached his heart and changed him.
🌙 **Conclusion:** True **knowledge leaves visible traces**. It reins in the tongue, guards the gaze, improves deeds, and beautifies character. If conduct remains unchanged, a person must examine what benefit his knowledge has actually brought him.

immutable.source: 📝 Ibn Mufliḥ al-Maqdisī, al-Ādāb ash-Sharʿiyyah, Bd. 2, S. 45; ebenso bei adh-Dhahabī, Siyar Aʿlām an-Nubalāʾ, Bd. 4, S. 583–584.
